text:
This has nothing to do with the 5070 as it (the 5070) is quite irrelevant.

Am I the only one who enables DLSS (or upscaling in games that do not support it), and limits framerates with their 4090 just to make sure it isn’t getting too much load? Using upscaling (Quality, any less is unnecessary), I notice that my 4090 uses quite a bit less power, and with upscaling, I never have to worry about my fps falling below 144 (I game at 1440p). I do my best to put most of my load on my cpu (5800X), as it will bottleneck my 4090, but in the titles I play, the 5800X is rarely ever maxed out when capped to 144. I think the closest it gets is running Halo Infinite, or Ratchet and Clank. Playing cyberpunk with DLSS quality, and RT Overdrive, it feels like i never fall below 144. Anyway, these are some of the things I think about when there’s nothing to think about and all the bills are paid. Picking up a broken 4090 back near launch (cracked pcb) was actually one of the best deals I ever made. a little over $800, and maybe 4-5 hours of labor made it so much more reasonable considering the most competition in that price point was the 7900XT, and the 4070 Ti. If you want to save yourself some money, pick up electronics repair and you’ll almost never be forced to pick up any new hardware if performance is your goal. Similar to buying cars, or other appliances. You can get a loan to get a used working one, or drop thousands on a used car, or you could drop a few hundred (depending on the model), diagnose whatever problems it has, and do it yourself! I don’t remember the last time I bought a new gpu (maybe an HD5550 way back in the early sc2 days), and I don’t forsee myself ever having to UNLESS AMD and Nvidia starts serializing their hardware (like apple).
